25654-stories-of-king-arthur-s-knights-t.creator: Unknown
25654-stories-of-king-arthur-s-knights-t.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Queen Guinevere lay idly in bed dreaming beautiful dreams. The sunny morning hours were slipping away, but she was so happy in dreamland, that she did not remember that her little maid had called her long ago.

62357-message-from-mars.title: Message From Mars
62357-message-from-mars.creator: Unknown
62357-message-from-mars.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. You don't think you'll go to Mars?" Scott shook his head. "I haven't lost my faith. Someone will get there ... But it's too soon yet. Look at that tablet, will you!" He waved his hand at a bronze plate set into the wall. "The roll of honor," said Scott, bitterly. You'll have to buy another soon. There won't be room enough." One Nixon already was on that scroll of bronze. Hugh Nixon, fifty-fourth from the top.

arxiv-2107-00965.title: Steady States of Holographic Interfaces
arxiv-2107-00965.creator: Constantin Bachas, Zhongwu Chen, Vassilis Papadopoulos
arxiv-2107-00965.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Constantin Bachas, Zhongwu Chen, Vassilis Papadopoulos. We find stationary thin-brane geometries that are dual to far-from-equilibrium steady states of two-dimensional holographic interfaces. The flow of heat at the boundary agrees with the result of CFT and the known energy-transport coefficients of the thin-brane model. We argue that by entangling outgoing excitations the interface produces coarse-grained entropy at a maximal rate, and point out similarities and differences with double-sided black funnels.

The Sloan Digital Sky Survey has recently initiated its 5th survey generation (SDSS-V), with a central focus on stellar spectroscopy.

arxiv-2208-14425.title: Fluctuation theory of continuous-time skip-free downward Markov chains with applications to branching processes with immigration
arxiv-2208-14425.creator: R. Loeffen, P. Patie, J. Wang
arxiv-2208-14425.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by R. Loeffen, P. Patie, J. Wang. We develop a new methodology for the fluctuation theory of continuous-time skip-free Markov chains, extending the recent work of Choi and Patie [ 6 ] for discrete-time skip-free Markov chains. As the main application we use it to derive a full set of fluctuation identities regarding exiting a finite or infinite interval for Markov branching processes with immigration, thereby uncovering many new results for this classical family of continuous-time Markov chains.

arxiv-2304-02993.title: Natural Language Robot Programming: NLP integrated with autonomous robotic grasping
arxiv-2304-02993.creator: Muhammad Arshad Khan, Max Kenney, Jack Painter, Disha Kamale † \dagger, Riza Batista-Navarro, Amir Ghalamzan E
arxiv-2304-02993.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a grammar-based natural language framework for robot programming, specifically for pick-and-place tasks. Our approach uses a custom dictionary of action words, designed to store together words that share meaning, allowing for easy expansion of the vocabulary by adding more action words from a lexical database.

arxiv-2304-11618.title: Modality-Aware Negative Sampling for Multi-modal Knowledge Graph Embedding
arxiv-2304-11618.creator: Yichi Zhang, Mingyang Chen, Wen Zhang †
arxiv-2304-11618.description: Abstract Negative sampling (NS) is widely used in knowledge graph embedding (KGE), which aims to generate negative triples to make a positive-negative contrast during training. However, existing NS methods are unsuitable when multi-modal information is considered in KGE models. They are also inefficient due to their complex design.

arxiv-2308-15629.title: Dynamic random intersection graph: Dynamic local convergence and giant structure
arxiv-2308-15629.creator: Marta Milewska, Remco van der Hofstad, Bert Zwart
arxiv-2308-15629.description: Abstract Random intersection graphs containing an underlying community structure are a popular choice for modelling real-world networks. Given the group memberships, the classical random intersection graph is obtained by connecting individuals when they share at least one group. We extend this approach and make the communities dynamic by letting them alternate between an active and inactive phase.

arxiv-2311-16587.title: Parameterized Inapproximability Hypothesis under ETH
arxiv-2311-16587.creator: Venkatesan Guruswami, Bingkai Lin, Xuandi Ren, Yican Sun, Kewen Wu
arxiv-2311-16587.description: Abstract The Parameterized Inapproximability Hypothesis (PIH) asserts that no fixed parameter tractable (FPT) algorithm can distinguish a satisfiable CSP instance, parameterized by the number of variables, from one where every assignment fails to satisfy an ε \varepsilon fraction of constraints for some absolute constant ε > 0 \varepsilon>0 . PIH plays the role of the PCP theorem in parameterized complexity.

arxiv-2401-03390.title: Global Prediction of COVID-19 Variant Emergence Using Dynamics-Informed Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2401-03390.creator: Majd Al Aawar, Srikar Mutnuri, Mansooreh Montazerin, Ajitesh Srivastava
arxiv-2401-03390.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Majd Al Aawar, Srikar Mutnuri, Mansooreh Montazerin, Ajitesh Srivastava. During the COVID-19 pandemic, a major driver of new surges has been the emergence of new variants. When a new variant emerges in one or more countries, other nations monitor its spread in preparation for its potential arrival. The impact of the new variant and the timings of epidemic peaks in a country highly depend on when the variant arrives.

arxiv-2404-06150.title: (Not) Understanding Latin Poetic Style with Deep Learning
arxiv-2404-06150.creator: Ben Nagy
arxiv-2404-06150.description: Abstract This article summarizes some mostly unsuccessful attempts to understand authorial style by examining the attention of various neural networks (LSTMs and CNNs) trained on a corpus of classical Latin verse that has been encoded to include sonic and metrical features.

arxiv-2501-05201.title: A study on the 1- � \Gamma inverse of tensors via the M-Product

arxiv-2501-05201.description: Abstract In this paper, we will study the issue about the 1- � \Gamma inverse, where � ∈ { † , D , ∗ } \Gamma\in\{{\dagger},\ D,\ *\} , via the M-product. The aim of the current study is threefold. Firstly, the definition and characteristic of the 1- � \Gamma inverse is introduced.

arxiv-2509-18922.title: Ultrasound response to time-reversal symmetry breaking below the superconducting phase transition
arxiv-2509-18922.creator: Chris Halcrow, Paul Leask, Egor Babaev
arxiv-2509-18922.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chris Halcrow, Paul Leask, Egor Babaev. Ultrasound attenuation is a powerful probe of symmetry-breaking phenomena in superconductors. In this work, we develop a framework to model the ultrasound response of multi-component superconductors undergoing a time-reversal symmetry breaking transition below the superconducting phase transition. By coupling the elastic strain of the crystal lattice to the superconducting order parameters through group-theoretical analysis of tetragonal crystals, we classify how different symmetry channels contribute to the ultrasound signal.

arxiv-2509-25669.title: GroundSight: Augmenting Vision-Language Models with Grounding Information and De-hallucination Conference: In Proceedings of 2025 KDD Cup Workship for Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation at the 31th ACM SGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDDCup’ 25); August 03–07, 2025; T
arxiv-2509-25669.creator: Xinxi Chen, Tianyang Chen, Lijia Hong
arxiv-2509-25669.description: Abstract . We propose a method to improve Visual Question Answering (VQA) with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by introducing text-grounded object localization. Rather than retrieving information based on the entire image, our approach enables the model to generate a bounding box around the object most relevant to the question, allowing for targeted image cropping and focused retrieval.

arxiv-2512-22130.title: Expert-Grounded Automatic Prompt Engineering for Extracting Lattice Constants of High-Entropy Alloys from Scientific Publications using Large Language Models
arxiv-2512-22130.creator: Shunshun Liu, Talon R. Booth, Yangfeng Ji, Wesley Reinhart, Prasanna V. Balachandran
arxiv-2512-22130.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for scientific data extraction from publications, but rely on manual prompt refinement. We present an expert-grounded automatic prompt optimization framework that enhances LLM entity extraction reliability. Using high-entropy alloy lattice constant extraction as a testbed, we optimized prompts for Claude 3.5 Sonnet through feedback cycles on seven expert-annotated publications.

pmc-10709385.title: Home-run trials for rare cancers: giving the right drug(s) to the right patients at the right time and in the right place
pmc-10709385.creator: Jacob J Adashek, Razelle Kurzrock
pmc-10709385.description: In oncology clinical trials, many patients spend their final months at a central clinical trial facility far from home for “mandatory” protocol visits/diagnostic testing. Studies suggest that the travel strain may be greatest among patients living in low‐income areas and/or participating in early-phase studies.

pmc-11650293.title: Using online attitudinal and completion test to understand the consumerś perception of probiotic dry-fermented sausage
pmc-11650293.creator: Marilia Silva Malvezzi Karwowski, Eliane Cristine Francisco-Maffezzolli, Evelin da Costa Boiko, Renata Ernlund Freitas de Macedo
pmc-11650293.description: This study aimed to assess consumer perceptions and the connections between consumers' health-related concerns and their perceptions of probiotic fermented sausage. The study was carried out using a 4-step online questionnaire composed of: (1) identification and recruitment; (2) application of the completion test; (3) attitudinal exploration; (4) socioeconomic inquiry.

pmc-12472915.title: The Role of Plectin Dysregulation in Cancer: Recent Advances
pmc-12472915.creator: Wenbin Wang, Chang Lyu, Zhihui Wang, Xu Zhang, Qing Luo, Guanbin Song, Gabriella Marucci
pmc-12472915.description: Plectin is a key cytolinker protein that functions as an integrator of the cytoskeletal networks by crosslinking intermediate filaments with actin filaments and microtubules. Mutations or function deficiencies of plectin lead to tissue disorders, particularly affecting the skin, muscle, and nervous tissues.

pmc-12562500.title: Roles of Deubiquitinases OTUD3 and OTUD5 in Inflammatory Bowel Diseases
pmc-12562500.creator: Tomohiro Watanabe, Masatoshi Kudo
pmc-12562500.description: Excessive production of type I interferons (IFNs) underlies the immunopathogenesis of autoimmune disorders, including systemic lupus erythematosus and autoimmune pancreatitis. Whether type I IFNs play pathogenic or protective roles in the development of inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) has been a matter of debate.

pmc-12606217.title: A software platform for real-time and adaptive neuroscience experiments
pmc-12606217.creator: Anne Draelos, Matthew D Loring, Maxim Nikitchenko, Chaichontat Sriworarat, Pranjal Gupta, Daniel Y Sprague, Eftychios Pnevmatikakis, Andrea Giovannucci, Tyler Benster, Karl Deisseroth, John M Pearson, Eva A Naumann
pmc-12606217.description: Current neuroscience research is often limited to testing predetermined hypotheses and post hoc analysis of already collected data. Adaptive experimental designs, in which modeling drives ongoing data collection and selects experimental manipulations, offer a promising alternative. However, such adaptive paradigms require tight integration between software and hardware under real-time constraints.

pmc-13359545.creator: Yuichiro Suzukawa, Yuto Tagawa, Seigo Katakura, Shuhei Teranishi, Tetsuro Kondo, Haruhiro Saito, Shuji Murakami
pmc-13359545.description: Simple SummaryComprehensive next-generation sequencing (NGS) has become the standard approach for the identification of actionable driver alterations in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, amplicon-based RNA sequencing may fail to detect ALK fusion genes in a small subset of cases because of technical limitations.

pmc-13382848.title: Leucettinib-21 decreases dosage effects of DYRK1A in human trisomy 21 induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neural cells
pmc-13382848.creator: Nicole R. West, Mattias F. Lindberg, Julien Dairou, Shawn MacGregor, Sahith Puthireddy, Laurent Meijer, Anita Bhattacharyya
pmc-13382848.description: Dosage imbalance of dual specificity tyrosine phosphorylation regulated kinase 1A (DYRK1A) is a feature of several neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative diseases, including Down syndrome, DYRK1A syndrome, autism spectrum disorders, Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease. Thus, manipulating DYRK1A activity in the brain has emerged as a potential therapeutic target for neurological disorders.
